I think you're missing the biggest one of all. The reason America's political system is failing so rapidly is in large part because of first past the post. Nearly all modern democracies now use some form of proportional voting. Proportional representation is great not only for getting valid representation, but also helping make sure the systems of checks and balances present in all governments actually work. I think the best way to point out the problem is by comparison.

Let's imagine we have a state with 100 representatives. The population of this state is spread uniformly with a distribution of about 29% republican 31% democrat, 15% libertarian, 15% socialist, 10% other.

So how do we pick our representatives? In the US with first past the post what we have to do is to cut up the state up into little arbitrary blocks of voters called districts. Each district now votes for one representative so for our state there will be 100 districts. First past the post is the most 'natural' sort of voting. We count up all the votes and whoever gets the most wins. Now since this state is uniformly distributed we know every single district is going to be 31% democrat, 29% republican, 15% libertarian, 15% socialist, and 10% other. In first past the post democrats will win every single district election. Even though they only have 31% of the people's support, they get 100% of the seats in first past the post.

Proportional representation is far more logical, simple, and fair. What happens is the people instead vote for their preferred party/person and the votes are tallied as a whole. In this case that means that we'll end up with 31 representatives being decided by the democrat party, 29 representatives being decided by the republican party, 15 for the libertarians and socialists, and so on. You end up with representation that's actually indicative of the political views of the state.

In first past the post, third parties simply do not win elections because they have to completely beat every other party in a single district. So even if non-democrats may make up 69% of the voters in our given state, they get 0% of the representation. First past the post also actually even encourages voters to vote against their own preferred candidate. Whether your political leaning is liberal or conservative you've likely had a vote at some point where wanted to vote for somebody who's views you really agree with but instead decided to vote for the "more electable" candidate because he's less terrible than if the candidate from the opposing party wins. This concept of "electability" is a unique problem with first past the post and massively empowers things like the media who can decide elections by painting certain candidates as non electable. In proportional systems you need not fear this as they only have to get sufficient votes to obtain a seat - not to beat every other party.
